producer_statement: EBP activity of amorolfine unmeasured in the sources reached
correction: Category stands for mammalian OPCs: Sax says amorolfine was 'previously established' to act by sterol 14-reductase inhibition in OPCs. BUT the suspected miss is real in fungi: amorolfine (phenylmorpholine) affects Erg24p (delta14 reductase) AND Erg2p (delta8-delta7 isomerase) (review abstract; an 1985 Candida study with Ro 14-4767/002 reports ignosterol accumulation 'indicating an inhibition of delta14-sterol reductase and delta8-delta7-isomerase'; a 2015 morpholine paper repeats the mode of action). Candida sterol-profile rows for amorolfine are also in ChEMBL (CHEMBL366). Yeast ERG2 and mammalian EBP are different proteins (INFERENZA from background; ChEMBL lists them as separate targets), so this does not transfer. Closest mammalian datum: the ChEMBL human-EBP Ki set (Laggner 2005, assay CHEMBL829736) includes fenpropimorph Ki 30 nM at human EBP, a close morpholine analogue of amorolfine, so an EBP effect of amorolfine is plausible but unmeasured (IPOTESI). Hubler's text says amorolfine and TASIN-1 doses 'led to accumulation of 14-dehydrozymostenol and zymostenol' without saying which sterol belongs to which compound: unverifiable from the text layer.
